description: How an error, a warning, and every other text written for a person is written on standard error, in the human text of atoll rules check and in the message of a disk's line of a human output: each character of the general category Cc or Cf, for which a name is written in base64 (shown_name.json), as \u{XXXX}, its code point in uppercase hexadecimal of four digits or more; each byte that is not UTF-8 as \x{XX}; and a backslash that u{ or x{ follows as \u{005C}, so that no backslash of the text reads as an escape. Anything else is written as it is: a text with none of these is unchanged, and so is what Go's %q, the quotes of a key of the configuration or systemd-escape escaped already. The --json outputs and the log hold the text as it is.

cases.text: configuration: disk[0].mount: the mount path does not exist
cases.shown: configuration: disk[0].mount: the mount path does not exist
cases.note: plain ASCII: as it is

cases.text: atoll : disque t1 : sa corbeille n'a pas pu être relue
cases.shown: atoll : disque t1 : sa corbeille n'a pas pu être relue
cases.note: a letter outside ASCII, of the French messages: as it is
U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE in a path an error from below the CLI writes as it is: written as it is, the line reads exe.mkv
U+202A LEFT-TO-RIGHT EMBEDDING
U+2066 LEFT-TO-RIGHT ISOLATE and U+2069 POP DIRECTIONAL ISOLATE, each on its own
U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE, which shows nothing
U+00AD SOFT HYPHEN, a format character too
U+FEFF ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE
U+1D173 MUSICAL SYMBOL BEGIN BEAM, past U+FFFF: five digits
U+E0001 LANGUAGE TAG, the last plane but one
a tab: four digits at least, as U+0009 writes it
a line feed: the error writes no line of its own
a carriage return, which would write over the line
an escape sequence that would clear a terminal
NUL
DEL
U+0085 NEXT LINE, a C1 control
a byte that is not UTF-8: two digits, as x{} says a byte
a sequence cut short: each of its bytes
U+D800 written as UTF-8 would be, which no UTF-8 holds: each byte
an overlong form of /: each byte, never /
U+FFFD REPLACEMENT CHARACTER itself, valid UTF-8 (So): as it is
U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR (Zl): as it is, as the maintainer chose (2026-11-22)
U+2029 PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR (Zp): as it is
U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE (Zs): as it is
U+034F COMBINING GRAPHEME JOINER (Mn): as it is
U+2065, unassigned in Unicode 17.0.0 (Cn): as it is
a backslash that no u{ or x{ follows: as it is
a backslash at the end: as it is
a backslash then u{, which would read as an escape: the backslash is written u{005C}
a backslash then x{: the same
a backslash before a character that is escaped: what follows it is a backslash, not u{, and it stays as it is
two backslashes then u{: the first, which a backslash follows, as it is, the second written u{005C}
what Go's %q escaped already, with no braces: as it is, never escaped twice
a key of the configuration, whose quotes escape it already (specs.md §24.3): as it is
a unit as systemd-escape writes it: as it is
U{ in uppercase is none of the escapes: as it is
u{ that no backslash comes before: as it is
nothing: as it is
